[Section: On the argument of those who interpreted "qurū'" (menstrual cycles/periods) as "purity periods" from this verse]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period (ʿiddah)﴾

The basis of the argument from it: the lām here is the lām of time, meaning: divorce them at the time of their waiting period, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya: 47], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection; and His saying: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra: 78], meaning: at the time of its decline.

The Arabs say: "I came to you for three nights remaining of the month," meaning: in three nights remaining of it. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained this verse with this interpretation. In the two Sahihs, it is reported from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that when he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to take her back, then divorce her while she is in a state of purity, before he has touched her. Then he (ﷺ) said: "That is the waiting period by which Allah commanded that women be divorced."

So the Prophet (ﷺ) clarified that the waiting period by which Allah commanded women to be divorced is the purity period that follows the menstrual period. Had the qurū' been menstruation, he would have divorced her before the waiting period, not during it, and that would have been a prolonging of her waiting, which is impermissible, just as if he had divorced her during menstruation.

[Section: The ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in agreement with the Book of Allah, that there is no maintenance (nafaqah) or housing (sukna) for the irrevocably divorced woman (al-mabtūtah)]

Muslim reported in his Sahih, from Fatimah bint Qays: that Abu ʿAmr ibn Hafs divorced her irrevocably (al-batta) while he was absent, and he sent to her his agent with barley, and she was displeased with it, so he said: "By Allah, you have no claim upon us for anything." So she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him and what he had said. He said: "You have no maintenance from him." He commanded her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Shurayk, then he said: "That is a woman whom my companions frequent. Observe your waiting period at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man; you may take off your clothes there. When you have completed it, inform me." She said: When I had completed it, I mentioned to him that Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for Abu Jahm, he does not put down his staff from his shoulder. As for Muʿawiyah, he is a pauper with no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd." I disliked him, then he said: "Marry Usamah ibn Zayd," so I married him, and Allah placed much good in him, and I was content.

Also in his Sahih, from her: that her husband divorced her during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had spent upon her a meagre maintenance. When she saw that, she said: "By Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If I am entitled to maintenance, I will take what suffices me, and if I am not entitled to maintenance, I will not take anything from him." She said: I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "You have no maintenance nor housing."

[Mention of the agreement of this ruling with the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic]

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period, and count the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter. And when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and bring to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah﴾ [at-Talaq: 1–2], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has set a measure for all things﴾ [at-Talaq: 1–3].

So Allah, glorified is He, commanded the husbands, for whom at the time of the term's reaching there is retention or release, that they should not expel their wives from their houses, and He commanded the wives that they should not leave. This indicates the permissibility of expelling one whom her husband no longer has the right to retain after the divorce. For He, glorified is He, mentioned for these divorced women rulings that are mutually connected, none of which is separated from another.

The first: that the husbands should not expel them from their houses.
The second: that they should not leave the houses of their husbands.
The third: that their husbands have the right to retain them in kindness before the end of the term, or to refrain from retaining them, and so release them with goodness.
The fourth: the calling of two just witnesses, which is witnessing the return (ar-raj'ah), either obligatorily or recommendedly. He, glorified is He, indicated the wisdom of this, and that it applies specifically to revocable divorces, by His saying: ﴿You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾.

The matter whose bringing about is hoped for here is the return (al-muraja'ah).

Thus said the early generation (al-salaf) and those after them. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us from Dawud al-Awdi, from al-Shaʿbi, regarding: ﴿You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: "Perhaps you will regret, and then there will be a path for you to return."

Al-Dahhak said regarding: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: "Perhaps he will take her back during the waiting period." This was also said by ʿAta', Qatadah and al-Hasan. And the statement of Fatimah bint Qays has already preceded: "What matter will come about after the three?"

This indicates that the divorce mentioned is the revocable one, in which these rulings are established, and that the wisdom of the All-Wise, the Most Merciful, required it: perhaps the husband will regret, and the evil that Satan incited between them will be removed, and his soul will incline toward her, so he takes her back. As ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If people had acted upon Allah's command concerning divorce, no man would ever have pursued his own soul to divorce a wife."

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the command to house these divorced women, saying: ﴿House them where you dwell, according to your means﴾ [at-Talaq: 6].

So the pronouns all share one referent, and their rulings are all mutually connected. The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Maintenance and housing are only for the woman when her husband has the right of return over her" was derived from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, explaining it and clarifying the intended meaning of its speaker. Thus the unity of the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has become clear, and the just balance is with both of them as well, not contradicting them. For maintenance is only due to a wife; when she is separated from him, she becomes a stranger, with the ruling of all other strangers, and nothing remains but her observing the waiting period from him, which does not make maintenance obligatory for her, like a woman who was involved by mistake or fornication. Moreover, maintenance is due only in exchange for the husband's ability to enjoy her, and this is impossible after her separation. Also, if maintenance were due to her because of her waiting period, it would be due to the widow from his estate, and there is absolutely no difference between them, for each of them has been separated from him while observing a waiting period from him, and enjoyment is impossible for both. Also, if housing were due to her, maintenance would be due to her as well, as the one who makes it obligatory says.

As for housing being due to her without maintenance, the text and analogy reject it. This is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas and his companions, Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, and Fatimah bint Qays, one of the jurists among the women of the Companions, and Fatimah used to argue for it. It is also the position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and his companions, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and his companions, Dawud ibn ʿAli and his companions, and all the people of hadith.

The jurists have three opinions on this question, and they are three narrations from Ahmad: the first is this one. The second: that she is entitled to both maintenance and housing, which is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Masʿud, and the jurists of Kufa. The third: that she is entitled to housing but not maintenance, which is the position of the people of Madinah, and it is the view of Malik and al-Shafiʿi.

(Lataifah – a subtle point)
An incident occurred in the days of Ibn Jarir: a man married a woman whom he loved intensely, while she hated him intensely, and she would confront him with insults and curses against him. One day he said to her: "You are divorced three times; you will not address me with anything except that I will address you with its like." She immediately said to him: "You are divorced three times, absolutely." The man was dumbfounded and did not know what to do, so he asked a group of jurists, and all of them said: "It is necessary that you divorce her, for if he responds to her with the like of her words, she is divorced, and if he does not respond, he has broken his oath and she is divorced. If he fulfills it, she is divorced, and if he breaks it, she is divorced." So he was directed to Ibn Jarir, who said to her: "Go, and do not repeat oaths. Remain with your wife, and after that say to her: 'You are divorced three times if I divorce you,' so you have addressed her with the like of her address to you, you have fulfilled your oath, and you have not divorced her, because of the condition attached to the divorce." He mentioned this to Ibn ʿAqil, who approved of it, and said: "There is another aspect Ibn Jarir did not mention: she said to him, 'Anta tāliq thalāthan' with a fatha on the taʾ, which is a masculine address. If he says to her 'Anta' with a fatha on the taʾ, no divorce falls."

I say: There is another aspect better than the two, and it follows the principles of the school, namely the specification of a general expression by intention. As when one swears not to have lunch and intends the lunch of that day, it is restricted to that. And if one swears not to speak to someone and intends by it speech that he dislikes, he does not break his oath if he speaks to him with what he likes, and its parallels are many. Based on this, the statement is explicit, or akin to explicit, in that he only intended: "Do not speak to me with insult, abuse, or cursing, or what is of this category, except that I will speak to you with its like." He did not intend that if she said to him, "Buy me a headscarf or a garment," he would say to her, "Buy me a garment or a headscarf." And if she said to him, "Do not buy me such-and-such, for I do not like it," he would say to her the like of this. This is something that definitively shows the swearer did not intend it. So if he does not address her with its like, he does not break his oath. Likewise, it is decisively shown that this case asked about was not intended by him, nor did the context of speech require it, nor did it occur to his mind; he only intended what was said that stirred his oath and prompted him to swear. Such a matter is taken into account by us in oaths.

(Fa'idah – a benefit)
Ibn ʿAqil was asked about a man whose wife said to him: "Divorce me." He said: "Allah has divorced you"?
He said: "The divorce takes effect, because it is an allusion (kinayah) supported by the indication of the situation, namely the mention of divorce and her request for it."
Some Shafiʿis answered that if he intended it, the divorce takes effect, otherwise it does not.
I say: This is the correct view. If his statement "Allah has divorced you" means that He legislated your divorce and permitted it, no divorce takes effect. But if he means that Allah has inflicted divorce upon you and willed and decreed it, then this would be a divorce, because it is necessarily true that the divorce has taken place; and when a statement admits both meanings, it does not take effect except with intention.

(Fa'idah)
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾
Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: "He will make for him a way out from every constriction upon people." Abu al-ʿAliyah said: "A way out from every hardship." This is comprehensive of the hardships and constrictions of this world and the Hereafter, for Allah makes for the God-fearing a way out from every constriction that is strait upon people and hard for them in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Hasan said: "A way out from what He forbade him."

(Fa'idah)
Ibn Majah and Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If all people acted upon this verse, it would suffice them."

(Fasl – a section)
Know that whoever fears Allah in his divorce, and divorces as Allah and His Messenger commanded and legislated for him, Allah will suffice him from all of that. For this reason, after mentioning the ruling of lawful divorce, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾.

Had the majority of divorcers feared Allah, they would have been independent through His piety from burdens and shackles, and from deceit and trickery. For the divorce that Allah, glorified is He, legislated is that he divorces her while she is in a state of purity without intercourse, divorces her once, and then leaves her until her waiting period ends. If it seems good to him to retain her during the waiting period, he retains her. If he does not return to her until her waiting period has ended, it is possible for her to remarry him anew without another husband. If he has no need for her, it does not harm him that she marries someone else. Whoever does this does not regret, and does not need a stratagem involving a husband or a legal marriage (tahlil).

For this reason, Ibn ʿAbbas was asked about a man who divorced his wife a hundred times. He said: "You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife is separated from you; you did not fear Allah, so He will not make a way out for you."

Said Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "A man came to Ibn ʿAbbas and said: 'I divorced my wife a thousand times.' He said: 'As for three, your wife is forbidden to you, and the rest are a burden of sin. You have taken the signs of Allah in mockery.'"

Mujahid said: "I was with Ibn ʿAbbas when a man came and said: 'He divorced his wife three times.' He remained silent, until I thought he would return her to him. Then he said: 'One of you goes and mounts the foolishness, then says: "O Ibn ʿAbbas, O Ibn ʿAbbas!" And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. And you have not feared Allah, so I find no way out for you. You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has separated from you.'" Narrated by Abu Dawud.

Al-Nasa'i narrated from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed about a man who divorced his wife with three pronouncements all at once. He stood up angry and said: 'Is the Book of Allah being played with while I am among you?' Until a man stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I not kill him?'"

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a decree for everything﴾

That is: sufficient for whoever trusts in Him in his calamities and affairs; He suffices him in all that concerns him. And "ḥasb" means sufficient, as in ﴿Allah is sufficient for us﴾, meaning Allah is our sufficiency.

Whenever a servant has a good opinion of Allah, good hope in Him, and sincere reliance upon Him, Allah will certainly not disappoint his hope in Him, for He, glorified is He, never disappoints the hope of one who hopes, nor wastes the work of one who works.

(Fa'idah)
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a decree for everything﴾

When He mentioned His sufficiency for the one who relies upon Him, this might give the impression of immediate sufficiency at the time of reliance, so He followed it with His saying: ﴿Allah has already set a decree for everything﴾, meaning a time from which it does not exceed. He drives it to the time He has ordained for it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 65, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 6)**

The one who relies upon God (*mutawakkil*) should not be hasty. He may say, "I have relied upon God and I have supplicated, but I have seen nothing, and my sufficiency has not been attained." Yet God brings about His command at the time He has decreed for it. This is very frequent in the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophetic way), and it is a subtle gateway to understanding the texts.

(Section)

Regarding reliance (*tawakkul*), He says: ﴿And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him.﴾

Consider this reward that the one who relies upon God receives, and that He has not assigned it to anyone else.

This indicates that reliance is the strongest of the means to God and the most beloved of them to Him. That God has entrusted affairs to Himself does not contradict the servant's reliance upon Him. Rather, this confirms that all affairs are entrusted to Him, because when the servant knows this and realizes it through knowledge, his state becomes reliance, definitely, upon the One whose affairs are such, since he knows that all affairs are entrusted to Him and that the servant owns none of them. Thus he has no choice but to depend upon Him, to commit his affairs to Him, and to trust in Him, for two reasons:

From the standpoint of his poverty and his not owning anything whatsoever.

And from the standpoint that the whole matter is in His hand and returns to Him.

Reliance arises from these two kinds of knowledge.

(Benefit)

Whoever occupies himself with God, away from himself, God will suffice him the burden of himself.

Whoever occupies himself with God, away from people, God will suffice him the burden of people.

Whoever occupies himself with himself, away from God, God will leave him to himself.

Whoever occupies himself with people, away from God, God will leave him to them.

(Benefit)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, God has set a measure for everything.﴾

Every created thing has a measure that God has set for it specifically. Measure (*qadar*, divine decree) is either a measure in knowledge or a measure in concrete existence.

The first is the measure of knowledge, which is the determining of a thing in knowledge, in speech, and in the Book, just as a servant determines in himself what he wants to say, write, and do, and so assigns it a measure.

Among this is God's determining of the measures of creatures in His knowledge and His Book before bringing them into existence, and then bringing them into being according to the measure He knew and recorded.

Thus the divine decree is of two kinds:

The first: in knowledge and in writing.

The second: the creating, originating, and fashioning of them by His power, by which He creates things.

Creation includes both origination and measuring together.

The point is that every originator has a measure, and the servants do not measure the Creator as He should be measured, and the disbelievers among them do not measure Him with the true measure. For this reason He, glorified is He, mentioned this only concerning them. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they did not measure God with His true measure when they said, "God has not sent down anything upon a human."﴾ [al-An'am: 91]

[Section: Reliance (*tawakkul*)]

Likewise the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions, on the Day of Uhud, when it was said to them after they had withdrawn from Uhud: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 173]

So they prepared and went out to meet their enemy, and they gave them the best of their souls. Then they said: ﴿Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 173]. The word had its effect and produced its consequence. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him.﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]

So He made reliance follow piety, which is the carrying out of the means that have been commanded. Then, if one relies upon God, He is sufficient for him. Likewise He said in another place: ﴿And fear God, and upon God let the believers rely.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 11]

Reliance and seeking sufficiency without carrying out the commanded means is pure incapacity. If it is mixed with some kind of reliance, then it is the reliance of incapacity. The servant should not make his reliance into incapacity, nor make his incapacity into reliance. Rather, he should make his reliance part of the commanded means, without which the goal is not achieved in its entirety.

Here two groups of people have erred. The first group claimed that reliance alone is an independent cause, sufficient for attaining the desired goal. So they nullified the means which the wisdom of God had established as leading to their results. They thus fell into a kind of negligence and incapacity, in proportion to what they nullified of the means. Their reliance grew weak, since they thought its strength lay in its isolation from the means. So they gathered all their concern and made it one concern. Although this has strength from one aspect, it has weakness from another. Whenever the side of reliance grows strong by being isolated, negligence regarding the means, which is the place of reliance, weakens it. For reliance has its place in the means, and its perfection lies in relying upon God within them. This is like the reliance of the farmer who tills the earth and casts the seed into it, then relies upon God for his crop and its growth. Such a one has given reliance its due, and his reliance is not weakened by leaving the land to lie barren. Likewise is the reliance of the traveler who crosses the distance while diligently journeying, and the reliance of the wise who seek salvation from God's punishment and success in His reward while striving in His obedience. This is the reliance that produces its effect, and God is sufficient for whoever stands by it.

As for the reliance of incapacity and negligence, its effect does not follow, and God is not sufficient for its possessor. God is only sufficient for the one who relies upon Him when he fears Him, and fear of Him is performing the commanded means, not wasting them.

The second group: those who stood by the means and saw the connection of the results with them, both legally and by decree, but turned away from the side of reliance. Although this group attained by what they did of the means what they attained, they do not have the strength of the people of reliance, nor God's help for them, His sufficiency for them, and His defense of them. Rather, they are forsaken and powerless, in proportion to what they lost of reliance.

So all strength lies in reliance upon God. As one of the early generations (*salaf*) said: Whoever wishes to be the strongest of people, let him rely upon God. Strength is guaranteed to the one who relies upon God, along with sufficiency, sufficing, and defense. What is lacking of this for him is only in proportion to what is lacking of piety and reliance. But if he truly attains both, God will surely make for him a way out of everything that is constricting for people, and God will be his sufficiency and sufficer.

The point is that the Prophet (ﷺ) guided the servant to that in which lies the utmost of his perfection and the attainment of his goal: that he should be eager for what benefits him, exert his effort in it, and then precaution (*tahassub*) will benefit him, and saying, "Sufficient for me is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." This is in contrast to the one who was incapable and negligent until his welfare escaped him, and then said, "Sufficient for me is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." For God blames him, and in this state He is not his sufficiency. He is only the sufficiency of the one who fears Him and relies upon Him.

[Divisions of stratagems (*hiyal*) and their levels]

[The first category of stratagems]

Section. The masters of stratagems say: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out.﴾

And stratagems are ways out of constrictions.

The response becomes clear only by mentioning a principle concerning the divisions of stratagems and their levels. So we say, and success is from God, that they are divisions.

[The first category of stratagems: covert means by which one reaches what is forbidden]

The first division: the hidden means by which one reaches what is itself forbidden, such that the means of that kind is never permissible in any circumstance. Whenever the aim of them is forbidden in itself, they are forbidden by the consensus of the Muslims. This includes stratagems for seizing people's wealth, wronging them in their persons, shedding their blood, nullifying their rights, and corrupting relations among them. These are of the same kind as the stratagems of the devils for leading the children of Adam astray by every path. The devils devise against them in order to bring them into one of six things, without fail. So they devise against them by every means to bring them into disbelief and hypocrisy, in their various kinds. If their stratagems succeed in that, their eyes are cooled. But if their stratagems fail with the one whose nature is sound and whom the witness of faith from his Lord follows, through the revelation that He sent down to His Messenger, they then employ stratagems to cast him into innovation (*bid'ah*), in its various kinds, and to make the heart accept it and prepare and dispose itself to it.

If their stratagems succeed, that is dearer to them than disobedience, even if it is a major sin. Then they look at the condition of whoever responded to them in innovation. If he is obeyed and followed among people, they order him to asceticism, worship, and good character and manners, then they spread praise of him among people in order to catch through him the ignorant and those who have no knowledge of the Sunnah. If he is not like that, they make his innovation a help to him in wronging the people of the Sunnah, harming them, and attacking them, and they make it appear to him that this is victory for the truth they hold. If this stratagem fails and God favors the servant by making him adhere to the Sunnah, knowing it, and distinguishing it from innovation, they cast him into major sins, make its commission appealing to him by every means, and say to him: You are upon the Sunnah. The sinful among the people of the Sunnah are friends of God, and the worshipers among the people of innovation are enemies of God. The graves of the sinful among the people of the Sunnah are a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and the graves of the worshipers among the people of innovation are a pit of the pits of the Fire. Adherence to the Sunnah expiates major sins, just as opposing the Sunnah nullifies good deeds. If the actions of the people of the Sunnah fall short, their beliefs stand by them, and if the actions of the people of innovation stand by them, their beliefs fall short.

The people of the Sunnah are those who thought well of their Lord, when they described Him with what He described Himself with and what His Messenger described Him with, and they described Him with every perfection and majesty and exalted Him above every deficiency. And God is according to His servant's assumption of Him. The people of innovation are those who assume evil of their Lord, since they deny Him the attributes of His perfection and declare Him transcendent above them. And when they deny Him those attributes, it necessarily follows that He is described by their opposites. For this reason God, exalted is He, said concerning one who denied a single one of His attributes, which is the attribute of knowledge in some particulars: ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ [Fussilat: 23]. He informed about those who assume evil of God that the circle of evil is upon them, that God is angry with them, has cursed them, and has prepared for them Hell, and evil is the destination. He did not threaten any with punishment more severely than one who assumed evil of Him. And you do not assume evil of Him, so what concern is punishment to you? Such are the truths they make into a means of connection for themselves and a stratagem toward belittling major sins and taking security for their own souls.

This stratagem is one from which none escapes except the firmly grounded in knowledge, who knows the names and attributes of God. For whenever one knows God more, he fears Him more, and whenever he is more ignorant of Him, he is more deluded about Him and less fearful.

If this stratagem fails and the majesty of God is great in the servant's heart, they make minor sins easy for him and say to him: They are expiated merely by avoiding major sins, so that it is as though they never happened. Perhaps they promise him that if he repents from them, whether they were major or minor sins, a good deed will be written for him in place of every bad deed. So they say to him: Multiply them as much as you can, then profit a good deed in place of every bad deed through repentance, even an hour before death. If this stratagem fails and God delivers His servant from it, they move him to the superfluities of permissible things and to indulging in them. They say to him: David had a hundred wives except one, then he wished to complete them to a hundred. Solomon, his son, had a hundred wives. Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Uthman ibn Affan had wealth that is well known. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and al-Layth ibn Sa'd had worldly goods and abundance of wealth that is not unknown. They make him forget the virtue of these people, and that they were not cut off from God by their worldly goods, but rather traveled with them toward Him, so that they became a path for them to God.

فَإنْ أعْجَزَتْهم هَذِهِ الحِيلَةُ، بِأنْ تَفْتَحَ بَصِيرَةَ قَلْبِ العَبْدِ حَتّى كَأنَّهُ يُشاهِدُ بِها الآخِرَةَ وما أعَدَّ اللَّهُ فِيها لِأهْلِ طاعَتِهِ وأهْلِ مَعْصِيَتِهِ، فَأخَذَ حَذَرَهُ، وتَأهَّبَ لِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِ، واسْتَقْصَرَ مُدَّةَ هَذِهِ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا في جَنْبِ الحَياةِ الباقِيَةِ الدّائِمَةِ، نَقَلُوهُ إلى الطّاعاتِ المَفْضُولَةِ الصَّغِيرَةِ الثَّوابِ لِيَشْغَلُوهُ بِها عَنِ الطّاعاتِ الفاضِلَةِ الكَثِيرَةِ الثَّوابِ، فَيُعْمِلُ حِيلَتَهُ في تَرْكِهِ كُلَّ طاعَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ إلى ما هو دُونَها، فَيُعْمِلُ حِيلَتَهُ في تَفْوِيتِ الفَضِيلَةِ عَلَيْهِ. فَإنْ أعْجَزَتْهم هَذِهِ الحِيلَةُ، وهَيْهاتَ، لَمْ يَبْقَ لَهم إلّا حِيلَةٌ واحِدَةٌ، وهي تَسْلِيطُ أهْلِ الباطِلِ والبِدَعِ والظَّلَمَةِ عَلَيْهِ يُؤْذُونَهُ، ويُنَفِّرُونَ النّاسَ عَنْهُ، ويَمْنَعُونَهم مِنَ الِاقْتِداءِ بِهِ؛ لِيُفَوِّتُوا عَلَيْهِ مَصْلَحَةَ الدَّعْوَةِ إلى اللَّهِ، وعَلَيْهِمْ مَصْلَحَةَ الإجابَةِ.

فَهَذِهِ مَجامِعُ أنْواعِ حِيَلِ الشَّيْطانِ، ولا يُحْصِي أفْرادَها إلّا اللَّهُ، ومَن لَهُ مُسْكَةٌ مِنَ العَقْلِ يَعْرِفُ الحِيلَةَ الَّتِي تَمَّتْ عَلَيْهِ مِن هَذِهِ الحِيَلِ، فَإنْ كانَتْ لَهُ هِمَّةٌ إلى التَّخَلُّصِ مِنها، وإلّا فَلْيَسْألْ مَن تَمَّتْ عَلَيْهِ، واللَّهُ المُسْتَعانُ.

[مِن حِيَلِ شَياطِينِ الإنْسِ]

وَهَذِهِ الحِيَلُ مِن شَياطِينِ الجِنِّ نَظِيرُ حِيَلِ شَياطِينِ الإنْسِ المُجادِلِينَ بِالباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الحَقَّ، ويَتَوَصَّلُوا بِهِ إلى أغْراضِهِمُ الفاسِدَةِ في الأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ والدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ، وذَلِكَ كَحِيَلِ القَرامِطَةِ البَاطِنِيَّةِ عَلى إفْسادِ الشَّرائِعِ، وحِيَلِ الرُّهْبانِ عَلى أشْباهِ الحَمِيرِ مِن عابِدِ الصَّلِيبِ بِما يُمَوِّهُونَ بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ المَخارِيقِ والحِيَلِ، كَالنُّورِ المَصْنُوعِ وغَيْرِهِ مِمّا هو مَعْرُوفٌ عِنْدَ النّاسِ، وكَحِيَلِ أرْبابِ الإشاراتِ مِنَ الإذْنِ والتَّسْيِيرِ والتَّغْيِيرِ وإمْساكِ الحَيّاتِ ودُخُولِ النّارِ في الدُّنْيا قَبْلَ الآخِرَةِ، وأمْثالِ ذَلِكَ مِن حِيَلِ أشْباهِ النَّصارى الَّتِي تَرُوجُ عَلى أشْباهِ الأنْعامِ، وكَحِيَلِ أرْبابِ الدَّكِّ وخِفَّةِ اليَدِ الَّتِي تَخْفى عَلى النّاظِرِينَ أسْبابُها ولا يَتَفَطَّنُونَ لَها، وكَحِيَلِ السَّحَرَةِ عَلى اخْتِلافِ أنْواعِ السِّحْرِ؛ فَإنَّ سِحْرَ البَيانِ هو مِن أنْواعِ التَّحَيُّلِ: إمّا لِكَوْنِهِ بَلَغَ مِنَ اللُّطْفِ والحُسْنِ إلى حَدِّ اسْتِمالَةِ القُلُوبِ فَأشْبَهَ السِّحْرَ مِن هَذا الوَجْهِ، وإمّا لِكَوْنِ القادِرِ عَلَى البَيانِ يَكُونُ قادِرًا عَلى تَحْسِينِ القَبِيحِ وتَقْبِيحِ الحَسَنِ، فَهو أيْضًا يُشْبِهُ السِّحْرَ مِن هَذا الوَجْهِ أيْضًا.

وَكَذَلِكَ سِحْرُ الوَهْمِ أيْضًا هو حِيلَةٌ وهْمِيَّةٌ، والواقِعُ شاهِدٌ بِتَأْثِيرِ الوَهْمِ والإيهامِ. أَلا تَرى أنَّ الخَشَبَةَ الَّتِي يَتَمَكَّنُ الإنْسانُ مِنَ المَشْيِ عَلَيْها إذا كانَتْ قَرِيبَةً مِنَ الأرْضِ لا يُمْكِنُ المَشْيُ عَلَيْها إذا كانَتْ عَلى مَهْواةٍ بَعِيدَةِ القَعْرِ؟ والأطِبّاءُ تَنْهى صاحِبَ الرُّعافِ عَنِ النَّظَرِ إلى الشَّيْءِ الأحْمَرِ، وتَنْهى المَصْرُوعَ عَنِ النَّظَرِ إلى الأشْياءِ القَوِيَّةِ اللَّمَعانِ أوِ الدَّوْرانِ، فَإنَّ النُّفُوسَ خُلِقَتْ مَطِيَّةَ الأوْهامِ، والطَّبِيعَةُ فَعّالَةٌ، والأحْوالُ الجُسْمانِيَّةُ تابِعَةٌ لِلْأحْوالِ النَّفْسانِيَّةِ.

وَكَذَلِكَ السِّحْرُ بِالِاسْتِعانَةِ بِالأرْواحِ الخَبِيثَةِ إنَّما هو بِالتَّحَيُّلِ عَلى اسْتِخْدامِها بِالإشْراكِ بِها والِاتِّصافِ بِهَيْئاتِها الخَبِيثَةِ؛ ولِهَذا لا يَعْمَلُ السِّحْرُ إلّا مَعَ الأنْفُسِ الخَبِيثَةِ المُناسِبَةِ لِتِلْكَ الأرْواحِ، وكُلَّما كانَتِ النَّفْسُ أخْبَثَ كانَ سِحْرُها أقْوى. وكَذَلِكَ سِحْرُ التَّمْزِيجاتِ، وهو أقْوى ما يَكُونُ مِنَ السِّحْرِ، أنْ يُمْزَجَ بَيْنَ القُوى النَّفْسانِيَّةِ الخَبِيثَةِ الفَعّالَةِ والقُوى الطَّبِيعِيَّةِ المُنْفَعِلَةِ. والمَقْصُودُ أنَّ السِّحْرَ مِن أعْظَمِ أنْواعِ الحِيَلِ الَّتِي يَنالُ بِها السّاحِرُ غَرَضَهُ، وحِيَلُ السّاحِرِ مِن أضْعَفِ الحِيَلِ وأقْواها، ولَكِنْ لا تُؤَثِّرُ تَأْثِيرًا مُسْتَقِرًّا إلّا في الأنْفُسِ الباطِلَةِ المُنْفَعِلَةِ لِلشَّهَواتِ، الضَّعِيفَةِ تَعَلُّقِها بِفاطِرِ الأرْضِ والسَّمَواتِ، المُنْقَطِعَةِ عَنِ التَّوَجُّهِ إلَيْهِ والإقْبالِ عَلَيْهِ؛ فَهَذِهِ النُّفُوسُ مَحَلُّ تَأْثِيرِ السِّحْرِ.

وَكَحِيَلِ أرْبابِ المَلاهِي والطَّرَبِ عَلى اسْتِمالَةِ النُّفُوسِ إلى مَحَبَّةِ الصُّوَرِ والوُصُولِ إلى الِالتِذاذِ بِها؛ فَحِيلَةُ السَّماعِ الشَّيْطانِيِّ عَلى ذَلِكَ مِن أدْنى الحِيَلِ عَلَيْهِ، حَتّى قِيلَ: أوَّلُ ما وقَعَ الزِّنا في العالَمِ فَإنَّما كانَ بِحِيلَةِ اليَراعِ والغِناءِ، لَمّا أرادَ الشَّيْطانُ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَجِدْ عَلَيْهِ حِيلَةً أدْنى مِنَ المَلاهِي.

وَكَحِيَلِ اللُّصُوصِ والسُّرّاقِ عَلى أخْذِ أمْوالِ النّاسِ، وهم أنْواعٌ لا تُحْصى؛ فَمِنهمُ السُّرّاقُ بِأيْدِيهِمْ، ومِنهمُ السُّرّاقُ بِأقْلامِهِمْ، ومِنهمُ السُّرّاقُ بِأمانَتِهِمْ، ومِنهمُ السُّرّاقُ بِما يُظْهِرُونَهُ مِنَ الدِّينِ والفَقْرِ والصَّلاحِ والزُّهْدِ وهم في الباطِنِ بِخِلافِهِ، ومِنهمُ السُّرّاقُ بِمَكْرِهِمْ وخِداعِهِمْ وغِشِّهِمْ. وبِالجُمْلَةِ فَحِيَلُ هَذا الضَّرْبِ مِنَ النّاسِ مِن أكْثَرِ الحِيَلِ، وتَلِيها حِيَلُ عُشّاقِ الصُّوَرِ عَلى الوُصُولِ إلى أغْراضِهِمْ، فَإنَّها تَقَعُ في الغالِبِ خَفِيَّةً، وإنَّما تَتِمُّ غالِبًا عَلى النُّفُوسِ القابِلَةِ المُنْفَعِلَةِ الشَّهْوانِيَّةِ. وكَحِيَلِ التَّتارِ الَّتِي مَلَكُوا بِها البِلادَ وقَهَرُوا بِها العِبادَ وسَفَكُوا بِها الدِّماءَ واسْتَباحُوا بِها الأمْوالَ، وكَحِيَلِ اليَهُودِ وإخْوانِهِمْ مِنَ الرّافِضَةِ، فَإنَّهم بَيْتُ المَكْرِ والِاحْتِيالِ، ولِهَذا ضُرِبَتْ عَلى الطّائِفَتَيْنِ الذِّلَّةُ، وهَذِهِ سُنَّةُ اللَّهِ في كُلِّ مُخادِعٍ مُحْتالٍ بِالباطِلِ.

[أرْبابُ الحِيَلِ نَوْعانِ]

ثُمَّ أرْبابُ هَذِهِ الحِيَلِ نَوْعانِ: نَوْعٌ يُقْصَدُ بِهِ حُصُولُ مَقْصُودِهِ، ولا يَظْهَرُ أنَّهُ حَلالٌ، كَحِيَلِ اللُّصُوصِ وعُشّاقِ الصُّوَرِ المُحَرَّمَةِ ونَحْوِهِما، ونَوْعٌ يُظْهِرُ صاحِبُهُ أنَّ مَقْصُودَهُ خَيْرٌ وصَلاحٌ ويُبْطِنُ خِلافَهُ.

وَأرْبابُ النَّوْعِ الأوَّلِ أسْلَمُ عاقِبَةً مِن هَؤُلاءِ؛ فَإنَّهم أتَوُا البُيُوتَ مِن أبْوابِها والأمْرَ مِن طَرِيقِهِ ووَجْهِهِ، وأمّا هَؤُلاءِ فَقَلَبُوا مَوْضُوعَ الشَّرْعِ والدِّينِ. ولَمّا كانَ أرْبابُ هَذا النَّوْعِ إنَّما يُباشِرُونَ الأسْبابَ الجائِزَةَ ولا يُظْهِرُونَ مَقاصِدَهُمْ، أعْضَلَ أمْرُهُمْ، وعَظُمَ الخَطْبُ بِهِمْ، وصَعُبَ الِاحْتِرازُ مِنهُمْ، وعَزَّ عَلى العالَمِ اسْتِنْقاذُ قَتْلاهُمْ، فاسْتُبِيحَتْ بِحِيَلِهِمُ الفُرُوجُ، وأُخِذَتْ بِها الأمْوالُ مِن أرْبابِها فَأُعْطِيَتْ لِغَيْرِ أهْلِها، وعُطِّلَتْ بِها الواجِباتُ، وضُيِّعَتْ بِها الحُقُوقُ، وعَجَّتِ الفُرُوجُ والأمْوالُ والحُقُوقُ إلى رَبِّها عَجِيجًا، وضَجَّتْ مِمّا حَلَّ بِها إلَيْهِ ضَجِيجًا. ولا يَخْتَلِفُ المُسْلِمُونَ أنَّ تَعْلِيمَ هَذِهِ الحِيَلِ حَرامٌ، والإفْتاءَ بِها حَرامٌ، والشَّهادَةَ عَلى مَضْمُونِها حَرامٌ، والحُكْمَ بِها مَعَ العِلْمِ بِحالِها حَرامٌ. والَّذِي جَوَّزُوا مِنها ما جَوَّزُوا مِنَ الأئِمَّةِ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يُظَنَّ بِهِمْ أنَّهم جَوَّزُوهُ عَلى وجْهِ الحِيلَةِ إلى المُحَرَّمِ، وإنَّما جَوَّزُوا صُورَةَ ذَلِكَ الفِعْلِ.

ثُمَّ إنَّ المُتَحَيِّلَ المُخادِعَ المَكّارَ أخَذَ صُورَةَ ما أفْتَوْا بِهِ فَتَوَسَّلَ بِهِ إلى ما مَنَعُوا مِنهُ، ورَكَّبَ ذَلِكَ عَلى أقْوالِهِمْ وفَتاواهُمْ، وهَذا فِيهِ الكَذِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وعَلَى الشّارِعِ. مِثالُهُ: أنَّ الشّافِعِيَّ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعالى، يُجَوِّزُ إقْرارَ المَرِيضِ لِوارِثِهِ، فَيَتَّخِذُهُ مَن يُرِيدُ أنْ يُوصِيَ لِوارِثِهِ وسِيلَةً إلى الوَصِيَّةِ لَهُ بِصُورَةِ الإقْرارِ.

وَيَقُولُ: هَذا جائِزٌ عِنْدَ الشّافِعِيِّ، وهَذا كَذِبٌ عَلَى الشّافِعِيِّ؛ فَإنَّهُ لا يُجَوِّزُ الوَصِيَّةَ لِلْوارِثِ بِالتَّحَيُّلِ عَلَيْها بِالإقْرارِ. فَكَذَلِكَ الشّافِعِيُّ يُجَوِّزُ لِلرَّجُلِ إذا اشْتَرى مِن غَيْرِهِ سِلْعَةً بِثَمَنٍ أنْ يَبِيعَهُ إيّاها بِأقَلَّ مِمّا اشْتَراها مِنهُ بِناءً عَلى ظاهِرِ السَّلامَةِ، ولا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ حِيلَةً عَلى بَيْعِ مِائَةٍ بِمِائَةٍ وخَمْسِينَ إلى سَنَةٍ. فاَلَّذِي يَسُدُّ الذَّرائِعَ يَمْنَعُ ذَلِكَ ويَقُولُ: هو يُتَّخَذُ حِيلَةً إلى ما حَرَّمَهُ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ، فَلا يَقْبَلُ إقْرارَ المَرِيضِ لِوارِثِهِ، ولا يَصِحُّ هَذا البَيْعُ. ولا سِيَّما فَإنَّ إقْرارَ المَرْءِ شَهادَةٌ عَلى نَفْسِهِ، فَإذا تَطَرَّقَ إلَيْها التُّهْمَةُ بَطَلَتْ كالشَّهادَةِ عَلى غَيْرِهِ. والشّافِعِيُّ يَقُولُ: أقْبَلُ إقْرارَهُ إحْسانًا لِلظَّنِّ بِالمُقِرِّ، وحَمْلًا لِإقْرارِهِ عَلى السَّلامَةِ، ولا سِيَّما عِنْدَ الخاتِمَةِ.

وَمِن هَذا البابِ احْتِيالُ المَرْأةِ عَلى فَسْخِ نِكاحِ الزَّوْجِ بِما يُعْلِمُهُ إيّاها أرْبابُ المَكْرِ والِاحْتِيالِ، بِأنْ تُنْكِرَ أنْ تَكُونَ أذِنَتْ لِلْوَلِيِّ، أوْ بِأنَّ النِّكاحَ لَمْ يَصِحَّ؛ لِأنَّ الوَلِيَّ أوِ الشُّهُودَ جَلَسُوا وقْتَ العَقْدِ عَلى فِراشِ حَرِيرٍ، أوِ اسْتَنَدُوا إلى وِسادَةِ حَرِيرٍ.

وَقَدْ رَأيْتُ مَن يَسْتَعْمِلُ هَذِهِ الحِيلَةَ إذا طَلَّقَ الزَّوْجُ امْرَأتَهُ ثَلاثًا، وأرادَ تَخْلِيصَهُ مِن عارِ التَّحْلِيلِ وشَنارِهِ، فَأرْشَدَهُ إلى القَدْحِ في صِحَّةِ النِّكاحِ بِفِسْقِ الوَلِيِّ أوِ الشُّهُودِ، فَلا يَصِحُّ الطَّلاقُ في النِّكاحِ الفاسِدِ. وقَدْ كانَ النِّكاحُ صَحِيحًا لَمّا كانَ مُقِيمًا مَعَها عِدَّةَ سِنِينَ، فَلَمّا أوْقَعَ الطَّلاقَ الثَّلاثَ فَسَدَ النِّكاحُ!

وَمِن هَذا احْتِيالُ البائِعِ عَلى فَسْخِ البَيْعِ بِدَعْواهُ أنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ بالِغًا وقْتَ العَقْدِ، أوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَشِيدًا، أوْ كانَ مَحْجُورًا عَلَيْهِ، أوْ لَمْ يَكُنِ المَبِيعُ مِلْكًا لَهُ ولا مَأْذُونًا لَهُ في بَيْعِهِ.

فَهَذِهِ الحِيَلُ وأمْثالُها لا يَرْتابُ مُسْلِمٌ في أنَّها مِن كَبائِرِ الإثْمِ وأقْبَحِ المُحَرَّماتِ، وهي مِنَ التَّلاعُبِ بِدِينِ اللَّهِ، واتِّخاذِ آياتِهِ هُزُوًا، وهي حَرامٌ مِن جِهَتِها في نَفْسِها لِكَوْنِها كَذِبًا وزُورًا، وحَرامٌ مِن جِهَةِ المَقْصُودِ بِها، وهو إبْطالُ حَقٍّ وإثْباتُ باطِلٍ؛ فَهَذِهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْسامٍ:

[الحِيَلُ المُحَرَّمَةُ عَلى ثَلاثَةِ أنْواعٍ]

أحَدُها: أنْ تَكُونَ الحِيلَةُ مُحَرَّمَةً ويُقْصَدُ بِها المُحَرَّمُ.

الثّانِي: أنْ تَكُونَ مُباحَةً في نَفْسِها ويُقْصَدُ بِها المُحَرَّمُ؛ فَيَصِيرُ حَرامًا تَحْرِيمَ الوَسائِلِ، كالسَّفَرِ لِقَطْعِ الطَّرِيقِ وقَتْلِ النَّفْسِ المَعْصُومَةِ.

وَهَذانِ القِسْمانِ تَكُونُ الحِيلَةُ فِيهِما مَوْضُوعَةً لِلْمَقْصُودِ الباطِلِ المُحَرَّمِ، ومُفْضِيَةً إلَيْهِ، كَما هي مَوْضُوعَةٌ لِلْمَقْصُودِ الصَّحِيحِ الجائِزِ ومُفْضِيَةٌ إلَيْهِ؛ فَإنَّ السَّفَرَ طَرِيقٌ صالِحٌ لِهَذا وهَذا.

الثّالِثُ: أنْ تَكُونَ الطَّرِيقُ لَمْ تُوضَعْ لِلْإفْضاءِ إلى المُحَرَّمِ، وإنَّما وُضِعَتْ مُفْضِيَةً إلى المَشْرُوعِ، كَالإقْرارِ والبَيْعِ والنِّكاحِ والهِبَةِ ونَحْوِ ذَلِكَ، فَيَتَّخِذُها المُتَحَيِّلُ سُلَّمًا وطَرِيقًا إلى الحَرامِ، وهَذا مُعْتَرَكُ الكَلامِ في هَذا البابِ، وهو الَّذِي قَصَدْنا الكَلامَ فِيهِ بِالقَصْدِ الأوَّلِ.

[نَوْعٌ رابِعٌ مِنَ الحِيَلِ يَنْقَسِمُ إلى ثَلاثَةِ أقْسامٍ يُقْصَدُ بِها أخْذُ حَقٍّ]

القِسْمُ الرّابِعُ: أنْ يُقْصَدَ بِالحِيلَةِ أخْذُ حَقٍّ أوْ دَفْعُ باطِلٍ، وهَذا القِسْمُ يَنْقَسِمُ إلى ثَلاثَةِ أقْسامٍ أيْضًا:

أحَدُها: أنْ يَكُونَ الطَّرِيقُ مُحَرَّمًا في نَفْسِهِ، وإنْ كانَ المَقْصُودُ بِهِ حَقًّا، مِثْلُ أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ عَلى رَجُلٍ حَقٌّ فَيَجْحَدَهُ، ولا يُبَيِّنُهُ لَهُ، فَيُقِيمَ صاحِبُهُ شاهِدَيْ زُورٍ يَشْهَدانِ بِهِ، ولا يَعْلَمانِ ثُبُوتَ ذَلِكَ الحَقِّ. ومِثْلُ أنْ يُطَلِّقَ الرَّجُلُ امْرَأتَهُ ثَلاثًا ويَجْحَدَ الطَّلاقَ، ولا يُبَيِّنُهُ لَها، فَتُقِيمَ شاهِدَيْنِ يَشْهَدانِ أنَّهُ طَلَّقَها، ولَمْ يَسْمَعا الطَّلاقَ مِنهُ. ومِثْلُ أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ عَلى رَجُلٍ دَيْنٌ، ولَهُ عِنْدَهُ وَدِيعَةٌ، فَيَجْحَدَ الوَدِيعَةَ، فَيَجْحَدَ هو الدَّيْنَ، أوْ بِالعَكْسِ، ويَحْلِفَ ما لَهُ عِنْدِي حَقٌّ، أوْ ما أوْدَعَنِي شَيْئًا، وإنْ كانَ يُجِيزُ هَذا مَن يُجِيزُ مَسْألَةَ الظَّفَرِ (masʾalat al-ẓafar، أي جواز أخذ الإنسان حقَّه من مال من عليه الحق دون علمه إذا ظفر به).

ومِثْلُ أنْ تَدَّعِيَ عَلَيْهِ المَرْأةُ كِسْوَةً أوْ نَفَقَةً ماضِيَةً كَذِبًا وباطِلًا، فَيُنْكِرَ أنْ تَكُونَ مَكَّنَتْهُ مِن نَفْسِها أوْ سَلَّمَتْ نَفْسَها إلَيْهِ، أوْ يُقِيمَ شاهِدَيْ زُورٍ أنَّها كانَتْ ناشِزًا؛ فَلا نَفَقَةَ لَها ولا كِسْوَةَ. ومِثْلُ أنْ يَقْتُلَ رَجُلٌ وَلِيَّهُ، فَيُقِيمَ شاهِدَيْ زُورٍ ولَمْ يَشْهَدا القَتْلَ، فَيَشْهَدا أنَّهُ قَتَلَهُ. ومِثْلُ أنْ يَمُوتَ مَوْرُوثُهُ، فَيُقِيمَ شاهِدَيْ زُورٍ أنَّهُ ماتَ وأنَّهُ وارِثُهُ، وهُما لا يَعْلَمانِ ذَلِكَ. ونَظائِرُهُ مِمَّنْ لَهُ حَقٌّ لا شاهِدَ لَهُ بِهِ، فَيُقِيمُ شاهِدَيْ زُورٍ يَشْهَدانِ لَهُ بِهِ؛ فَهَذا يَأْثَمُ عَلَى الوَسِيلَةِ دُونَ المَقْصُودِ، وفي مِثْلِ هَذا جاءَ الحَدِيثُ: «أدِّ الأمانَةَ إلى مَن ائْتَمَنَكَ، ولا تَخُنْ مَن خانَكَ».

[فَصْلٌ: القِسْمُ الثّانِي مِن أنْواعِ الحِيَلِ]

فَصْلٌ: القِسْمُ الثّانِي: أنْ يَكُونَ الطَّرِيقُ مَشْرُوعَةً، وما يُفْضِي إلَيْهِ مَشْرُوعٌ، وهَذِهِ هي الأسْبابُ الَّتِي نَصَبَها الشّارِعُ مُفْضِيَةً إلى مُسَبَّباتِها كالبَيْعِ والإجارَةِ والمُساقاةِ والمُزارِعَةِ والوَكالَةِ، بَلْ الأسْبابُ مَحَلُّ حُكْمِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ، وهي في اقْتِضائِها لِمُسَبَّباتِها شَرْعًا عَلى وِزانِ الأسْبابِ الحِسِّيَّةِ في اقْتِضائِها لِمُسَبَّباتِها قَدَرًا؛ فَهَذا شَرْعُ الرَّبِّ تَعالى وذَلِكَ قَدَرُهُ، وهُما خَلْقُهُ وأمْرُهُ، واللَّهُ لَهُ الخَلْقُ والأمْرُ، ولا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ، ولا تَغْيِيرَ لِحُكْمِهِ، فَكَما لا يُخالِفُ سُبْحانَهُ بِالأسْبابِ القَدَرِيَّةِ أحْكامَها بَلْ يُجْرِيها عَلى أسْبابِها وما خُلِقَتْ لَهُ؛ فَهَكَذا الأسْبابُ الشَّرْعِيَّةُ لا يُخْرِجُها عَنْ سَبَبِها وما شُرِعَتْ لَهُ، بَلْ هَذِهِ سُنَّتُهُ شَرْعًا وأمْرًا، وتِلْكَ سُنَّتُهُ قَضاءً وقَدَرًا، وسُنَّتُهُ الأمْرِيَّةُ قَدْ تُبَدَّلُ وتَتَغَيَّرُ كَما يُعْصى أمْرُهُ ويُخالَفُ، وأمّا سُنَّتُهُ القَدَرِيَّةُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا ولَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا، كَما لا يُعْصى أمْرُهُ الكَوْنِيُّ القَدَرِيُّ.

وَيَدْخُلُ في هَذا القِسْمِ التَّحَيُّلُ عَلى جَلْبِ المَنافِعِ وعَلى دَفْعِ المَضارِّ، وقَدْ ألْهَمَ اللَّهُ تَعالى ذَلِكَ لِكُلِّ حَيَوانٍ؛ فَلِأنْواعِ الحَيَواناتِ مِن أنْواعِ الحِيَلِ والمَكْرِ ما لا يَهْتَدِي إلَيْهِ بَنُو آدَمَ.

وَلَيْسَ كَلامُنا ولا كَلامُ السَّلَفِ في ذَمِّ الحِيَلِ مُتَناوِلًا لِهَذا القِسْمِ. بَلْ العاجِزُ مَن عَجَزَ عَنْهُ، والكَيِّسُ مَن كانَ بِهِ أفْطَنَ وعَلَيْهِ أقْدَرَ، ولا سِيَّما في الحَرْبِ فَإنَّها خَدْعَةٌ. والعَجْزُ كُلُّ العَجْزِ تَرْكُ هَذِهِ الحِيلَةِ. والإنْسانُ مَندُوبٌ إلى اسْتِعاذَتِهِ بِاللَّهِ تَعالى مِن العَجْزِ والكَسَلِ؛ فالعَجْزُ عَدَمُ القُدْرَةِ عَلى الحِيلَةِ النّافِعَةِ. والكَسَلُ عَدَمُ الإرادَةِ لِفِعْلِها؛ فالعاجِزُ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ الحِيلَةَ، والكَسْلانُ لا يُرِيدُها. ومَن لَمْ يَحْتَلْ وقَدْ أمْكَنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الحِيلَةُ أضاعَ فُرْصَتَهُ وفَرَّطَ في مَصالِحِهِ، كَما قالَ:

؎إذا المَرْءُ لَمْ يَحْتَلْ وقَدْ جَدَّ جِدُّهُ ∗∗∗ أضاعَ وقاسى أمْرَهُ وهو مُدْبِرُ

وَفِي هَذا قالَ بَعْضُ السَّلَفِ: الأمْرُ أمْرانِ: أمْرٌ فِيهِ حِيلَةٌ فَلا يُعْجَزُ عَنْهُ، وأمْرٌ لا حِيلَةَ فِيهِ فَلا يُجْزَعُ مِنهُ.

[فَصْلٌ: القِسْمُ الثّالِثُ مِن أنْواعِ الحِيَلِ]
[المِثالُ الأوَّلُ: اسْتَأْجَرَ مِنهُ دارًا مُدَّةَ سِنِينَ بِأُجْرَةٍ مَعْلُومَةٍ فَخافَ أنْ يَغْدِرَ بِهِ المُكْرِي في آخِرِ المُدَّةِ]

فَصْلٌ: [الِاحْتِيالُ عَلى الوُصُولِ إلى الحَقِّ بِطَرِيقٍ مُباحَةٍ لَكِنَّها لَمْ تُشْرَعْ لَهُ].

القِسْمُ الثّالِثُ: أنْ يَحْتالَ عَلى التَّوَصُّلِ إلى حَقٍّ أوْ عَلى دَفْعِ الظُّلْمِ بِطَرِيقٍ مُباحَةٍ لَمْ تُوضَعْ مُوَصِّلَةً إلى ذَلِكَ، بَلْ وُضِعَتْ لِغَيْرِهِ، فَيَتَّخِذُها هو طَرِيقًا إلى هَذا المَقْصُودِ الصَّحِيحِ، أوْ قَدْ يَكُونُ قَدْ وُضِعَتْ لَهُ لَكِنْ تَكُونُ خَفِيَّةً ولا يَفْطِنُ لَها، والفَرْقُ بَيْنَ هَذا القِسْمِ والَّذِي قَبْلَهُ أنَّ الطَّرِيقَ في الَّذِي قَبْلَهُ نُصِبَتْ مُفْضِيَةً إلى مَقْصُودِها ظاهِرًا، فَسالِكُها سالِكٌ لِلطَّرِيقِ المَعْهُودِ، والطَّرِيقُ في هَذا القِسْمِ نُصِبَتْ مُفْضِيَةً إلى غَيْرِهِ فَيَتَوَصَّلُ بِها إلى ما لَمْ تُوضَعْ لَهُ؛ فَهي في الفِعالِ كالتَّعْرِيضِ الجائِزِ في المَقالِ، أوْ تَكُونُ مُفْضِيَةً إلَيْهِ لَكِنْ بِخَفاءٍ، ونَذْكُرُ لِذَلِكَ أمْثِلَةً يُنْتَفَعُ بِها في هَذا البابِ.

المِثالُ الأوَّلُ: إذا اسْتَأْجَرَ مِنهُ دارًا مُدَّةَ سِنِينَ بِأُجْرَةٍ مَعْلُومَةٍ، فَخافَ أنْ يَغْدِرَ بِهِ المُكْرِي في آخِرِ المُدَّةِ ويَتَسَبَّبَ إلى فَسْخِ الإجارَةِ بِأنْ يَظْهَرَ أنَّهُ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ وِلايَةُ الإيجارِ، أوْ أنَّ المُؤَجَّرَ مِلْكٌ لِابْنِهِ أوْ امْرَأتِهِ، أوْ أنَّهُ كانَ مُؤَجَّرًا قَبْلَ إيجارِهِ، ويَتَبَيَّنُ أنَّ المَقْبُوضَ أُجْرَةُ المِثْلِ لِما اسْتَوْفاهُ مِن المُدَّةِ، ويَنْتَزِعُ المُؤَجَّرَ لَهُ مِنهُ؛ فالحِيلَةُ في التَّخَلُّصِ مِن هَذِهِ الحِيلَةِ أنْ يُضَمِّنَهُ المُسْتَأْجِرُ دَرَكَ العَيْنِ المُؤَجَّرَةِ لَهُ أوْ لِغَيْرِهِ، فَإذا اسْتُحِقَّتْ أوْ ظَهَرَتْ الإجارَةُ فاسِدَةً رَجَعَ عَلَيْهِ بِما قَبَضَهُ مِنهُ، أوْ يَأْخُذُ إقْرارَ مَن يَخافُ مِنهُ بِأنَّهُ لا حَقَّ لَهُ في العَيْنِ، وأنَّ كُلَّ دَعْوى يَدَّعِيها بِسَبَبِها فَهي باطِلَةٌ، أوْ يَسْتَأْجِرُها مِنهُ بِمِائَةِ دِينارٍ مَثَلًا ثُمَّ يُصارِفَهُ كُلَّ دِينارٍ بِعَشَرَةِ دَراهِمَ، فَإذا طالَبَهُ بِأُجْرَةِ المِثْلِ طالَبَهُ هو بِالدَّنانِيرِ الَّتِي وقَعَ عَلَيْها العَقْدُ، فَإنَّهُ لَمْ يَخَفْ مِن ذَلِكَ، ولَكِنْ يَخافُ أنْ يَغْدِرَ بِهِ في آخِرِ المُدَّةِ، فَلْيُقَسِّطْ مَبْلَغَ الأُجْرَةِ عَلى عَدَدِ السِّنِينَ، ويَجْعَلْ مُعْظَمَها لِلسَّنَةِ الَّتِي يَخْشى غَدْرَهُ فِيها.

وَكَذَلِكَ إذا خافَ المُؤَجِّرُ أنْ يَغْدِرَ المُسْتَأْجِرُ ويَرْحَلَ في آخِرِ المُدَّةِ، فَلْيَجْعَلْ مُعْظَمَ الأُجْرَةِ عَلى المُدَّةِ الَّتِي يَأْمَنُ فِيها مِن رَحِيلِهِ، والقَدْرَ اليَسِيرَ مِنها لِآخِرِ المُدَّةِ.

[المِثالُ السّابِعُ: تَزَوُّجُ المَرْأةِ بِشَرْطِ ألّا يَتَزَوَّجَ عَلَيْها]

تَزَوُّجُ المَرْأةِ بِشَرْطِ ألّا يَتَزَوَّجَ عَلَيْها] المِثالُ السّابِعُ: إذا خاصَمَتْهُ امْرَأتُهُ وقالَتْ: قُلْ: "كُلُّ جارِيَةٍ أشْتَرِيها فَهي حُرَّةٌ، وكُلُّ امْرَأةٍ أتَزَوَّجُها فَهي طالِقٌ"، فالحِيلَةُ في خَلاصِهِ أنْ يَقُولَ ذَلِكَ ويَعْنِي بِالجارِيَةِ السَّفِينَةَ، لِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنّا لَمّا طَغى الماءُ حَمَلْناكم في الجارِيَةِ﴾ [الحاقة: ١١] (أي: إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في السفينة)، ويُمْسِكُ بِيَدِهِ حَصاةً أوْ خِرْقَةً ويَقُولُ: "فَهي طالِقٌ"، فَيَرُدُّ الكِنايَةَ إلَيْها، فَإنْ تَفَقَّهَتْ عَلَيْهِ الزَّوْجَةُ وقالَتْ: قُلْ: "كُلُّ رَقِيقَةٍ أوْ أمَةٍ"، فَلِيَقُلْ ذَلِكَ ولْيَعْنِ: فَهي حُرَّةُ الخِصالِ غَيْرُ فاجِرَةٍ، فَإنَّهُ لَوْ قالَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ تُعْتَقْ، كَما لَوْ قالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ: "غُلامُك فاجِرٌ زانٍ"، فَقالَ: ما أعْرِفُهُ إلّا حُرًّا عَفِيفًا، ولَمْ يُرِدْ العِتْقَ، لَمْ يُعْتَقْ.

وَإنْ تَفَقَّهَتْ عَلَيْهِ وقالَتْ: قُلْ: "فَهي عَتِيقَةٌ"، فَلِيَقُلْ ذَلِكَ ولِيَنْوِ ضِدَّ الجَدِيدَةِ، أيْ عَتِيقَةٌ في الرِّقِّ، فَإنْ تَفَقَّهَتْ وقالَتْ: قُلْ: "فَهي مَعْتُوقَةٌ" و"قَدْ أعْتَقْتها إنْ مَلَكْتها"، فَلْيَرُدَّ الكِنايَةَ إلى حَصاةٍ في يَدِهِ أوْ خِرْقَةٍ، فَإنْ لَمْ تَدَعْهُ أنْ يُمْسِكَ شَيْئًا فَلْيَرُدَّها إلى نَفْسِهِ، ويَعْنِي أنْ قَدْ أعْتَقَها مِن النّارِ بِالإسْلامِ، أوْ فَهي حُرَّةٌ لَيْسَتْ رَقِيقَةً لِأحَدٍ، ويَجْعَلُ الكَلامَ جُمْلَتَيْنِ، فَإنْ حَضَرَتْهُ وقالَتْ: قُلْ: "فالجارِيَةُ الَّتِي أشْتَرِيها مَعْتُوقَةٌ"، فَلْيُقَيِّدْ ذَلِكَ بِزَمَنٍ مُعَيَّنٍ، أوْ مَكانٍ مُعَيَّنٍ في نِيَّتِهِ، ولا يَحْنَثْ بِغَيْرِهِ، فَإنْ حَضَرَتْهُ وقالَتْ: مِن غَيْرِ تَوْرِيَةٍ ولا كِنايَةٍ ولا نِيَّةٍ تُخالِفُ قَوْلِي، وهَذا آخِرُ التَّشْدِيدِ، فَلا يَمْنَعُهُ ذَلِكَ مِن التَّوْرِيَةِ والكِنايَةِ.

وَإنْ قالَ بِلِسانِهِ: "لا أُوَرِّي ولا أُكَنِّي"، والتَّوْرِيَةُ والكِنايَةُ في قَلْبِهِ، كَما لَوْ قالَ: "لا أسْتَثْنِي" بِلِسانِهِ ومِن نِيَّتِهِ الِاسْتِثْناءُ، ثُمَّ اسْتَثْنى فَإنَّهُ يَنْفَعُهُ، حَتّى لَوْ لَمْ يَنْوِ الِاسْتِثْناءَ ثُمَّ عَزَمَ عَلَيْهِ واسْتَثْنى نَفَعَهُ ذَلِكَ بِالسُّنَّةِ الصَّحِيحَةِ الصَّرِيحَةِ الَّتِي لا مُعارِضَ لَها بِوَجْهٍ في غَيْرِ حَدِيثٍ، كَقَوْلِ المَلَكِ لِسُلَيْمانَ: قُلْ إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ، وقَوْلِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): «إلّا الإذْخِرَ» بَعْدَ أنْ ذَكَّرَهُ بِهِ العَبّاسُ، وقَوْلِهِ: «إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ» بَعْدَ أنْ قالَ: «لَأغْزُوَنَّ قُرَيْشًا، ثَلاثَ مَرّاتٍ»، ثُمَّ قالَ بَعْدَ الثّالِثَةِ وسُكُوتِهِ: «إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ».

والقُرْآنُ صَرِيحٌ في نَفْعِ الِاسْتِثْناءِ إذا نَسِيَهُ ولَمْ يَنْوِهِ في أوَّلِ كَلامِهِ ولا أثْناءَهُ، في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إنِّي فاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا * إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ واذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إذا نَسِيتَ﴾ [الكهف: ٢٣-٢٤]، وهَذا إمّا أنْ يَخْتَصَّ بِالِاسْتِثْناءِ إذا نَسِيَهُ كَما فَسَّرَهُ بِهِ جُمْهُورُ المُفَسِّرِينَ، أوْ يَعُمَّهُ ويَعُمَّ غَيْرَهُ وهو الصَّوابُ؛ فَأمّا أنْ يُخْرِجَ مِنهُ الِاسْتِثْناءَ الَّذِي سِيقَ الكَلامُ لِأجْلِهِ ويَرُدَّ إلى غَيْرِهِ فَلا يَجُوزُ، ولِأنَّ الكَلامَ الواحِدَ لا يُعْتَبَرُ في صِحَّتِهِ نِيَّةُ كُلِّ جُمْلَةٍ مِن جُمَلِهِ وبَعْضٍ مِن أبْعاضِهِ؛ فالنَّصُّ والقِياسُ يَقْتَضِي نَفْعَ الِاسْتِثْناءِ، وإنْ خَطَرَ لَهُ بَعْدَ انْقِضاءِ الكَلامِ، وهَذا هو الصَّوابُ المَقْطُوعُ بِهِ.

[المِثالُ الثّالِثَ عَشَرَ: الحِيلَةُ في التَّخَلُّصِ مِن طَلاقِ امْرَأتِهِ]
حِيلَةٌ في التَّخَلُّصِ مِن طَلاقِ امْرَأتِهِ]

المِثالُ الثّالِثَ عَشَرَ: إذا قالَ الرَّجُلُ لِامْرَأتِهِ: "الطَّلاقُ يَلْزَمُنِي لا تَقُولِينَ لِي شَيْئًا إلّا قُلْت لَك مِثْلَهُ"، فَقالَتْ لَهُ: أنْتَ طالِقٌ ثَلاثًا.

فالحِيلَةُ في التَّخَلُّصِ مِن أنْ يَقُولَ لَها مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ أنْ يَقُولَ لَها: قُلْت لِي: أنْتَ طالِقٌ ثَلاثًا.

قالَ أصْحابُ الشّافِعِيِّ: وفي هَذِهِ الحِيلَةِ نَظَرٌ لا يَخْفى؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَقُلْ لَها مِثْلَ ما قالَتْ لَهُ، وإنَّما حَكى كَلامَها مِن غَيْرِ أنْ يَقُولَ لَها نَظِيرَهُ. ولَوْ أنَّ رَجُلًا سَبَّ رَجُلًا فَقالَ لَهُ المَسْبُوبُ: "أنْتِ قُلْت لِي كَذا وكَذا"، لَمْ يَكُنْ قَدْ رَدَّ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَ أحَدٍ، لا لُغَةً ولا عُرْفًا؛ فَهَذِهِ الحِيلَةُ لَيْسَتْ بِشَيْءٍ.

وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى: الحِيلَةُ أنْ يَقُولَ لَها: "أنْتَ طالِقٌ ثَلاثًا" بِفَتْحِ التّاءِ، فَلا تَطْلُقُ، وهَذا نَظِيرُ ما قالَتْ لَهُ سَواءٌ، وهَذِهِ وإنْ كانَتْ أقْرَبَ مِن الأُولى؛ فَإنَّ المَفْهُومَ المُتَعارَفَ لُغَةً وعَقْلًا وعُرْفًا مِن الرَّدِّ عَلى المَرْأةِ أنْ يُخاطِبَها خِطابَ المُؤَنَّثِ، فَإذا خاطَبَها خِطابَ المُذَكَّرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ رَدًّا ولا جَوابًا، ولَوْ فُرِضَ أنَّهُ رَدٌّ لَمْ يَمْنَعْ وُقُوعَ الطَّلاقِ بِالمُواجَهَةِ وإنْ فَتَحَ التّاءَ، كَأنَّهُ قالَ: أيُّها الشَّخْصُ أوْ الإنْسانُ.

وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى: الحِيلَةُ في ذَلِكَ أنْ يَقُولَ: أنْتِ طالِقٌ ثَلاثًا إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ، أوْ إنْ كَلَّمْت السُّلْطانَ، أوْ إنْ سافَرْت، ونَحْوَ ذَلِكَ؛ فَيَكُونَ قَدْ قالَ لَها نَظِيرَ ما قالَتْ، ولا يَضُرُّهُ زِيادَةُ الشَّرْطِ، وهَذِهِ الحِيلَةُ أقْرَبُ مِن الَّتِي قَبْلَها، ولَكِنْ في كَوْنِ المُتَكَلِّمِ بِها رادًّا أوْ مُجِيبًا نَظَرٌ لا يَخْفى؛ لِأنَّ الشَّرْطَ وإنْ تَضَمَّنَ زِيادَةً في الكَلامِ لَكِنَّهُ يُخْرِجُهُ عَنْ كَوْنِهِ نَظِيرًا لِكَلامِها، ومِثْلًا لَهُ، وهو إنّما حَلَفَ أنْ يَقُولَ لَها مِثْلَ ما قالَتْ لَهُ، والجُمْلَةُ الشَّرْطِيَّةُ لَيْسَتْ مِثْلَ الجُمْلَةِ الخَبَرِيَّةِ، بَلْ الشَّرْطُ يَدْخُلُ عَلى الكَلامِ التّامِّ فَيُصَيِّرُهُ ناقِصًا يَحْتاجُ إلى الجَوابِ، ويَدْخُلُ عَلى الخَبَرِ فَيَقْلِبُهُ إنْشاءً، ويُغَيِّرُ صُورَةَ الجُمْلَةِ الخَبَرِيَّةِ ومَعْناها، ولَوْ قالَ رَجُلٌ لِغَيْرِهِ: "لَعَنَك اللَّهُ"، فَقالَ لَهُ: "لَعَنَك اللَّهُ إنْ بَدَّلْت دِينَك أوْ ارْتَدَدْت عَنْ الإسْلامِ"، لَمْ يَكُنْ سابًّا لَهُ.

وَلَوْ قالَ لَهُ: "يا زانٍ"، فَقالَ: "بَلْ أنْتَ زانٍ إنْ وطِئْت فَرْجًا حَرامًا"، لَمْ يَكُنْ الثّانِي قاذِفًا لَهُ. ولَوْ بَذَلَتْ لَهُ مالًا عَلى أنْ يُطَلِّقَها، فَقالَ: أنْتِ طالِقٌ إنْ كَلَّمْت السُّلْطانَ، لَمْ يَسْتَحِقَّ المالَ، ولَمْ يَكُنْ مُطَلِّقًا.

وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى: لا حاجَةَ إلى شَيْءٍ مِن ذَلِكَ، والحالِفُ لَمْ تَدْخُلْ هَذِهِ الصُّورَةُ في عُمُومِ كَلامِهِ، وإنْ دَخَلَتْ فَهي مِن المَخْصُوصِ بِالعُرْفِ والعادَةِ والعَقْلِ؛ فَإنَّهُ لَمْ يُرِدْ هَذِهِ الصُّورَةَ قَطْعًا، ولا خَطَرَتْ بِبالِهِ، ولا تَناوَلَها لَفْظُهُ؛ فَإنَّهُ إنّما تَناوَلَ لَفْظُهُ القَوْلَ الَّذِي يَصِحُّ "أنْتِ امْرَأتِي"، وبِمَنزِلَةِ قَوْلِ الأمَةِ لِسَيِّدِها: "أنْتَ أمَتِي وجارِيَتِي"، ونَحْوِ هَذا مِن الكَلامِ اللَّغْوِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَدْخُلْ تَحْتَ لَفْظِ الحالِفِ ولا إرادَتِهِ، أمّا عَدَمُ دُخُولِهِ تَحْتَ إرادَتِهِ فَلا إشْكالَ فِيهِ، وأمّا عَدَمُ تَناوُلِ لَفْظِهِ لَهُ؛ فَإنَّ اللَّفْظَ العامَّ إنّما يَكُونُ عامًّا فِيما يَصْلُحُ لَهُ وفِيما سِيقَ لِأجْلِهِ.

وَهَذا أقْوى مِن جَمِيعِ ما تَقَدَّمَ، وغايَتُهُ تَخْصِيصُ العامِّ بِالعُرْفِ والعادَةِ، وهَذا أقْرَبُ لُغَةً وعُرْفًا وعَقْلًا وشَرْعًا مِن جَعْلِ ما تَقَدَّمَ مُطابِقًا ومُماثِلًا لِكَلامِها مِثْلَهُ، فَتَأمَّلْهُ، واللَّهُ المُوَفِّقُ.

[المِثالُ الرّابِعَ عَشَرَ: الإحْرامُ وقَدْ ضاقَ الوَقْتُ]
[الإحْرامُ وقَدْ ضاقَ الوَقْتُ]

المِثالُ الرّابِعَ عَشَرَ: إذا خافَ الرَّجُلُ لِضِيقِ الوَقْتِ أنْ يُحْرِمَ بِالحَجِّ فَيَفُوتَهُ فَيَلْزَمَهُ القَضاءُ ودَمُ الفَواتِ؛ فالحِيلَةُ أنْ يُحْرِمَ إحْرامًا مُطْلَقًا ولا يُعَيِّنَهُ؛ فَإنِ اتَّسَعَ لَهُ الوَقْتُ جَعَلَهُ حَجًّا أوْ قِرانًا أوْ تَمَتُّعًا، وإنْ ضاقَ عَلَيْهِ الوَقْتُ جَعَلَهُ عُمْرَةً، ولا يَلْزَمُهُ غَيْرُها.

[المِثالُ الخامِسَ عَشَرَ: مَن جاوَزَ المِيقاتَ غَيْرَ مُحْرِمٍ]
[مَن جاوَزَ المِيقاتَ غَيْرَ مُحْرِمٍ]

**Example 15: If someone passes the mīqāt without being in ihrām, he is obliged to enter ihrām and to pay a dam (a penalty sacrifice) for passing the mīqāt without ihrām. The stratagem for removing the dam from him is that he should not enter ihrām from his present location but should return to the mīqāt and enter ihrām from there. If he enters ihrām from his present location, the dam is obligatory on him, and it does not fall away by his returning to the mīqāt.**

[Example 16: A stratagem for fulfilling an oath]
[A stratagem for fulfilling an oath]

**Example 16: If his property is stolen, and he says to his wife, "If you do not tell me who took it, you are divorced three times," while the wife does not know who took it, the stratagem for escaping this oath is that she should mention the persons from whom the taken item could not have come, and then name each one individually, saying, "He took it." In this way she informs about the taker and about others, so she fulfils her oath and is not divorced.**

[Example 42: The stratagem for the oath-taker not to break his oath]
[A stratagem for the oath-taker not to break his oath]

**Example 42: If someone is made to swear about something, and he wishes to swear without breaking the oath, the stratagem is that he moves his tongue with the words "in shā' Allāh" (God willing). Is it required that he make himself hear it? It has been said: he must make himself hear it. Our shaykh (Ibn Taymiyyah) said: there is no evidence for this. Rather, whenever he moves his tongue with it, he is speaking, even if he does not make himself hear it. The same ruling applies to obligatory sayings and obligatory recitation. I say: some of the early generations (salaf) would close their lips and move their tongues with "there is no god but God," remembering God, without making themselves hear it. The lips have no role in the letters of this phrase; rather, all of its letters are produced in the throat and by the tongue. So the one who remembers God can move his tongue with it without making himself or anyone else hear it, and no one sees him speaking. Likewise, one can say "in shā' Allāh" with the mouth closed, so no one hears or sees it. But if he closes his teeth and opens his lips slightly, his ears will hear the whole of it.**

[Example 55: A stratagem for nullifying testimony of adultery]
[A stratagem for nullifying testimony of adultery]

**Example 55: If a man is brought before the ruler (imām) and is accused of having committed adultery, and he fears that if he denies it, the evidence (bayyinah) will be established against him and he will be punished with the prescribed penalty (ḥadd), then the stratagem for nullifying their testimony is that he should confess when asked only once and not add anything to it. Then the evidence is not heard along with the confession. The judge or the ruler has no right to press him to complete the required quorum (niṣāb). Rather, if he remains silent, he is not pursued. If the ruler is one who holds that the ḥadd is obligatory on the basis of a single confession, then the stratagem is that he retracts his confession, so the ḥadd falls away from him. If he fears that evidence will be established against him, he confesses again and then retracts, and so on repeatedly. This stratagem is permissible, for it is lawful for him to ward off the ḥadd from himself and to turn to repentance, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Companions when Mā'iz fled from the ḥadd: "Why did you not leave him, so that he might repent and God might accept his repentance?" So if he flees from the ḥadd to repentance, he has done well.**

[Example 56: The stratagem for escape from breaking an oath]
[A stratagem for escape from breaking an oath]

**Example 56: If someone swears to a traitor, a spy, or a thief that he will not inform anyone about him and will not point him out, and he then wishes to free himself from this oath without concealing him, the stratagem is that he asks about groups of people of which he himself is one. When he is asked about someone other than himself, he says, "No." When the questioning reaches him, he remains silent. He does not break his oath, and he does not sin by concealing him and sheltering him. Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, was asked about this very same case. The questioner said to him: "Robbers came to me, took my property, and made me swear by divorce that I would not inform anyone about them. So I went out and saw them selling my goods openly in the market." Abū Ḥanīfah said to him: "Go to the governor and tell him to gather the people of the quarter or the street in which they are, and then have them brought before him. Then he will ask you about them one by one. If he asks you about someone who is not one of them, say, 'He is not one of them.' And if he asks you about someone who is one of them, remain silent." The man did so, and the governor took his goods from them and returned them to him. But if this stratagem were used with a wronged person, it would not benefit him, and the oath-taker would break his oath, because the purpose is to protect him, and by remaining silent he has actually helped against him and has not protected him.**

[Example 57: The stratagem for a husband and wife who both swear oaths]
[A stratagem for a husband and wife who both swear oaths]

**Example 57: This is what Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, was asked about: a husband said to his wife, "You are divorced if you ask me for khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation) and I do not grant you khul'." The wife said, "Every slave I own is free if I do not ask you for khul' today." The husband came to Abū Ḥanīfah and said, "Bring the woman." She was brought, and Abū Ḥanīfah said to her, "Ask him for khul'." She said, "I ask you to grant me khul'." Abū Ḥanīfah said to him, "Say to her: 'I have granted you khul' for a thousand dirhams, which you will give me.'" He said this to her. He then said to her, "Say: 'I do not accept.'" She said, "I do not accept." He said, "Now both of you stand with your spouse. Each of you has fulfilled his or her oath and has not broken it in any respect." Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan mentioned this in his book Kitāb al-Ḥiyal.

This stratagem is only complete in the form he described. If she had said to him, "I ask you for khul' for a thousand dirhams, payable immediately or within a month," and he had said, "I have granted you khul' on that basis," the khul' would take effect. This is unlike when she says to him, "Grant me khul'," and he says, "I have granted you khul' for a thousand," for this is not a khul' until she accepts and agrees, and she has not agreed to the thousand, so the khul' does not take effect.

[If it is said: then how is it that the khul' did not take effect?]

It is said: he swore about his own action, not about her acceptance. So when he says, "I have granted you khul' for a thousand," the khul' has occurred from his side, so his oath is resolved. The resolution of the oath does not depend on her acceptance, just as if someone swears that he will not sell, then sells, and the buyer does not accept and there is no evidence for it: he has broken his oath.

**Example 58: Two brothers, each of whom was given the other's wife in marriage**

[Two brothers, each of whom was given the other's wife in marriage]

**Example 58: What Muḥammad also mentioned in his book from him: two brothers came to him, each of whom had married one of two sisters. Each woman was escorted to the husband of her sister. Each husband consummated the marriage without knowing. Then, when they woke up in the morning, they realized the situation, told him about it, and asked him for a way out. He said to them, "Is each of you content with the one he consummated with?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Let each of you divorce the wife with whom he contracted the marriage, with one divorce." They did so. He said, "Let each of you now contract marriage with the woman with whom he consummated." They did so. He said, "Let each of you go to his own family." This stratagem is extremely subtle: each of them had had intercourse with the woman by mistake, so he may marry her during her waiting period ('iddah), since his water may not be kept from his own water. He ordered him to divorce only once, because he had not consummated with the woman whom he divorced; one divorce is irrevocable, and she has no 'iddah from him, so the other may marry her.

**Example 59: The stratagem for a woman to free herself from a husband she does not want**

[A stratagem for a woman to free herself from a husband she does not want]

**Example 59: If a woman marries and fears that her husband will travel and leave her, or will take her with him when she does not want to leave her home, or will take another wife or a concubine, or will drink intoxicants, or will beat her without fault, or will turn out to be poor when she had thought him wealthy, or defective when she had thought him sound, or illiterate when she had thought him a reciter, or ignorant when she had thought him learned, or something similar, and she cannot free herself, then the stratagem for her in all of these cases is that she stipulates in the contract that whenever any of these things occurs, her affair is in her own hand: if she wishes, she may remain with him, and if she wishes, she may separate from him. She should have witnesses to this condition. If she fears that after the contract becomes binding he will not accept this condition, she should not permit her guardian to marry her to him except on this condition. He should say, "I marry you both on the condition that her affair is in her hand if such-and-such happens." Whenever this condition is met, she has the right to divorce herself. There is no harm in this stratagem, for a woman frees herself through it from a marriage to someone she did not agree to, and she is spared from bringing her case to a judge so that he may annul her marriage on grounds of absence, poverty, or similar causes.

**Example 61: The stratagem for escaping from what the tongue has uttered**

[A stratagem for escaping from what the tongue has uttered]

**Example 61: If someone's tongue slips into saying something for which he would be held accountable outwardly, though he did not intend its meaning, or he intended it and then retracted and repented of it, or he feared that false witnesses would testify against him for it although he did not say it, and he is brought before the judge and accused of it, then if he denies it, the witnesses testify against him, and if he confesses, the judge rules against him. This is especially so if the judge does not consider repentance from such a thing to be accepted. The stratagem for escape is that he should neither confess nor deny it, so that the witnesses testify against him. Rather, it is enough for him to answer by saying, "If I said it, then I have retracted it, and I repent to God from it." The judge has no right after this to say, "I will not accept this answer from you; you must either confess or deny." This is a sufficient answer in such a claim. To require him after this to choose between confession, which may be false, or denial when he has already repented before God, and the witnesses then testify against him, is injustice and falsehood. So it is not permitted for the judge to ask him after this whether he did or did not do it. Even more so, if he is testified against for apostasy and says, "I have always testified that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God since I came to reason until now," he is not questioned further about anything, and neither he nor the witnesses are asked about the cause of his apostasy, as al-Khiraqī mentioned in his Mukhtaṣar and other companions of al-Shāfi'ī. So if he is accused of saying such-and-such, and he says, "If I said it, then I repent to God from it," or "I have repented from it," he is satisfied with this answer, and nothing further is probed after that.

**Example 82: A stratagem for not breaking an oath**

[A stratagem for not breaking an oath]

**Example 82: If a man swears by divorce that he will not guarantee anything for anyone, and another man swears by divorce that you must guarantee for me, then the stratagem for the first man to guarantee for him without breaking his oath is that he should become his partner and buy goods jointly with his partner.**

The judge (al-Qāḍī) said: he guarantees half the price on behalf of his partner, and the oath-taker does not break his oath, because what he swore about was the act of guaranteeing, and what he is obligated to in our case is not obligated by the contract of guarantee; rather, he is obligated by agency (wakālah), because each of the two partners is the agent of the other regarding what he buys. For this reason he does not break his oath. If the situation is as it is, but there is no partnership between him and the one he swore about, and he appointed him as an agent to buy, he likewise does not break his oath, for the reason we have explained.

**Example 84: The wronged person's stratagem to get people to revile the wrongdoer**

[The wronged person's stratagem to get people to revile the wrongdoer]

Example eighty-four: There is no harm for the wronged person to contrive, through people's reviling of his oppressor, the cursing and invoking of evil upon him, and taking from his honor, even if he does not do so himself; for perhaps that will deter him and prevent him from persisting in his oppression. This is like when he takes his property and he wears the most tattered clothes after the finest, and displays weeping, wailing and groaning; or when he harms him in his neighborhood so that he leaves his house and throws his belongings onto the road; or when he takes his beast so that he throws down its load on the road and sits weeping, and the like. All of this is among the things that call people to curse the oppressor, revile him and invoke evil upon him. The Prophet ﷺ had guided the wronged person harmed by his neighbor to something of this sort. In the Sunan and in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "A man complained to the Prophet ﷺ about his neighbor, and he said: 'Go and be patient.' He came to him twice or three times, and he said: 'Go and throw your belongings onto the road.' So he threw his belongings onto the road, and people began to ask him, and he informed them of his story, so the people began to curse him: 'May Allah do this to him and do that to him.' His neighbor came to him and said to him: 'Return; you will not see from me anything you dislike.'" This is the wording of Abu Dawud.

[Example eighty-five from the subtle stratagems of Abu Hanifah]
[From the subtle stratagems of Abu Hanifah]
Example eighty-five: It is mentioned in the virtues of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, that a man came to him at night and said: "Help me before dawn, or I will divorce my wife." He said: "What is that?" He said: "She left my speech tonight. I said to her: 'If dawn rises and you do not speak to me, then you are divorced three times.' I have implored her by every means to speak to me, but she has not done so." He said to him: "Go and order the muezzin of the mosque to come down and call the adhan before dawn, for perhaps when she hears it she will speak to you. And go to her and beseech her to speak to you before the muezzin calls." The man did so; he sat beseeching her, and the muezzin called the adhan. She said: "Dawn has risen and I am free of you." He said: "You have spoken to me before dawn, and I am released from the oath." This is among the finest stratagems.

[Another stratagem of his]
Example eighty-six: Bishr ibn al-Walid said: There was a young man in the neighborhood of Abu Hanifah who frequented his gathering. He said to him one day: "I want to marry a woman, and they have asked of me a dowry beyond my capacity, and I have become attached to the woman." He said to him: "Give them what they asked of you." He did so, and when the contract was concluded he came to him and said: "They have asked me for the dowry." He said: "Borrow and take a loan and give it to them." He did so. When he entered upon his wife, he said: "I fear the creditors, and I do not have what I can repay them with." He said: "Show that you intend a distant journey, and that you intend to leave with your family." He did so and hired camels, and this grieved the woman and her guardians. They came to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, and asked him, and he said: "He may take his family wherever he wishes." They said: "We will satisfy him and return to him what we took from him, and he will not travel." When the husband heard this he became greedy and said: "No, by Allah, not until they give me more." He said to him: "If you are content with this, well; otherwise, the woman will acknowledge that she owes a debt to a man, and then you cannot take her out until you pay it." He said: "By Allah, let not the family of the woman hear that from you; I am content with what I have given them."

[Section: stratagems are of three kinds]
The stratagems of this chapter are of three kinds: a stratagem to repel oppression and deception so that it does not occur; a stratagem to remove it after it has occurred; and a stratagem to respond to it with its like where it cannot be removed. The first two kinds are permissible, while the third requires detail. It cannot be said that it is permissible absolutely, nor that it is forbidden absolutely. Rather, if the means used against him is prohibited as a right of Allah, it is not permissible to respond to it with its like, as when someone makes him drink wine or commits fornication with his womenfolk. If it is prohibited because it is an injustice to him in his property, and he is able to oppress him in a similar way, this is the matter of "victory" (al-zafar), and some have been excessive in it, to the point of permitting the uprooting of a door, the breaching of a wall, the tearing of a ceiling and the like, in order to respond by taking an equivalent of his property. Others have prohibited it entirely, and said: If he has a deposit with him or a debt owed to him, it is not permissible for him to collect from him the amount of his right except by informing him of it. Others took a middle course and said: If the cause of the right is apparent, such as marriage, paternity, filiation, or ownership by right of possession that obliges maintenance, then he may take the amount of his right without informing him; but if it is not apparent, such as a loan, the price of a sold item and the like, he may not take it except by informing him. This is the most just of the opinions on the matter, and the Sunnah clearly indicates it; and those who hold it are most fortunate in it. And success is from Allah.

If it is slander against him, lying about him, defamation of him, or false testimony against him, it is not permissible for him to respond with its like. If it is a supplication against him, a curse, or reviling, then he may respond with its like according to the more correct of the two opinions, though many people prohibit it. If it is the destruction of property belonging to him: if that property is sacred, such as a slave or an animal, it is not permissible for him to respond with its like; and if it is not sacred, then if he fears that the other will exceed the bounds regarding it, it is not permissible for him to respond with its like, just as if he burned his house he may not burn his house. And if he does not exceed the bounds in it, but rather does to him the exact same thing that he did to him, such as cutting his tree, breaking his vessel, opening a cage on his bird, untying the mouth of a liquid container belonging to him, or releasing water onto his flat roof so that what is in it is lost, and the like, and he is able to respond with exactly what he did, then this is a matter of ijtihad (independent reasoning) on which neither the Book, nor the Sunnah, nor consensus, nor sound analogy indicates prohibition; rather, the cited evidences require its permissibility, as was previously explained at the beginning of the book.

Our shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, used to prefer this and say: "It is more deserving of permissibility than destroying his limb in return for his limb." And Allah knows best.

[Section: On the argument of those who interpreted "qurū'" (menstrual cycles/periods) as "purity periods" from this verse]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period (ʿiddah)﴾

The basis of the argument from it: the lām here is the lām of time, meaning: divorce them at the time of their waiting period, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya: 47], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection; and His saying: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra: 78], meaning: at the time of its decline.

The Arabs say: "I came to you for three nights remaining of the month," meaning: in three nights remaining of it. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained this verse with this interpretation. In the two Sahihs, it is reported from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that when he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to take her back, then divorce her while she is in a state of purity, before he has touched her. Then he (ﷺ) said: "That is the waiting period by which Allah commanded that women be divorced."

So the Prophet (ﷺ) clarified that the waiting period by which Allah commanded women to be divorced is the purity period that follows the menstrual period. Had the qurū' been menstruation, he would have divorced her before the waiting period, not during it, and that would have been a prolonging of her waiting, which is impermissible, just as if he had divorced her during menstruation.

[Section: The ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in agreement with the Book of Allah, that there is no maintenance (nafaqah) or housing (sukna) for the irrevocably divorced woman (al-mabtūtah)]

Muslim reported in his Sahih, from Fatimah bint Qays: that Abu ʿAmr ibn Hafs divorced her irrevocably (al-batta) while he was absent, and he sent to her his agent with barley, and she was displeased with it, so he said: "By Allah, you have no claim upon us for anything." So she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him and what he had said. He said: "You have no maintenance from him." He commanded her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Shurayk, then he said: "That is a woman whom my companions frequent. Observe your waiting period at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man; you may take off your clothes there. When you have completed it, inform me." She said: When I had completed it, I mentioned to him that Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for Abu Jahm, he does not put down his staff from his shoulder. As for Muʿawiyah, he is a pauper with no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd." I disliked him, then he said: "Marry Usamah ibn Zayd," so I married him, and Allah placed much good in him, and I was content.

Also in his Sahih, from her: that her husband divorced her during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he had spent upon her a meagre maintenance. When she saw that, she said: "By Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If I am entitled to maintenance, I will take what suffices me, and if I am not entitled to maintenance, I will not take anything from him." She said: I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "You have no maintenance nor housing."

[Mention of the agreement of this ruling with the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic]

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period, and count the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter. And when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and bring to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah﴾ [at-Talaq: 1–2], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has set a measure for all things﴾ [at-Talaq: 1–3].

So Allah, glorified is He, commanded the husbands, for whom at the time of the term's reaching there is retention or release, that they should not expel their wives from their houses, and He commanded the wives that they should not leave. This indicates the permissibility of expelling one whom her husband no longer has the right to retain after the divorce. For He, glorified is He, mentioned for these divorced women rulings that are mutually connected, none of which is separated from another.

The first: that the husbands should not expel them from their houses.
The second: that they should not leave the houses of their husbands.
The third: that their husbands have the right to retain them in kindness before the end of the term, or to refrain from retaining them, and so release them with goodness.
